source.title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory

accepted.question_text: In a Bell-type correlation experiment with N subsystems, M measurement choices per subsystem, and K outcomes per measurement, characterize exactly the measured probability tables that admit a classical local realistic joint probability distribution over all NM observables. Equivalently, describe the convex polyhedron generated by all classical configurations in terms of linear Bell inequalities; for tractable cases, find complete solutions for small triples (N, M, K), efficient methods for generating genuinely new inequalities, infinite or symmetry-restricted families, full-correlation-function versions, correlation inequalities for K = 2, and the margins by which such inequalities can be violated by quantum states, possibly under constraints such as fixed Hilbert-space dimension, symmetry, or positive partial transposes.
accepted.context_brief: Bell inequalities for finite correlation experiments

evidence.quote: Find all those linear inequalities characterizing the existence of joint probability distributions for all variables in a correlation experiment.
More specifically, suppose that measurements are made on systems, which are decomposed into N subsystems. On each of these subsystems one out of M observables is measured, producing K outcomes each.

Decide by what margin these can be violated by quantum states, or by quantum states with special properties (e. g., fixed Hilbert space dimension, invariance under symmetry transformations or positive partial transposes).

accepted.question_text: For bipartite quantum states, a state is distillable if sufficiently many copies can be converted by local quantum operations and classical communication into an approximation of a maximally entangled singlet state. States with positive partial transpose are known not to be distillable. Is the converse true: must every undistillable bipartite state have positive partial transpose?
accepted.context_brief: Distillability versus positive partial transpose

evidence.quote: A state on a bipartite quantum system is called distillable, if from sufficiently many pairs prepared in that state one can obtain a close approximation of a maximally entangled singlet state, using only local quantum operations and classical communication (LOCC). It is well-known that states with positive partial transpose (PPT) are not distillable. The problem is to decide the converse.

accepted.question_text: For bipartite quantum states, call two density operators equally entangled when they differ only by local choices of basis, meaning there are local unitaries UA and UB with rho = (UA tensor UB) sigma (UA tensor UB)*. A polynomial entanglement invariant is a real-valued local-unitary invariant polynomial in the matrix elements of the density operator. Are polynomial entanglement invariants complete, so that if all polynomial invariants of rho and sigma agree, rho and sigma must be related by such local unitaries?
accepted.context_brief: Completeness of polynomial entanglement invariants

evidence.quote:
The basic problem is to decide the following question:
• Are the polynomial entanglement invariants complete?,
i. e., if all polynomial invariants of ρ and σ agree, can we infer the existence of unitaries UA, UB satisfying the above equation?
The basic question of principle (are the polynomial entanglement invariants complete?) is answered in Onishchik and Vinberg’s book Lie Groups and Algebraic Groups

accepted.question_text: For local-unitary entanglement invariants, determine finite complete sets of polynomial invariants for specified Alice and Bob Hilbert-space dimensions, extend the problem to multipartite states including pure multipartite states, and decide whether separability can be characterized, or at least usefully approximated by necessary or sufficient criteria, using a polynomial invariant f with f(rho) >= 0 corresponding to separability, possibly with f depending on the dimensions.
accepted.context_brief: Finite invariant sets and separability via polynomial invariants

evidence.quote:
But we may add some further, closely related problems:
• Given the dimensions of Alices’s and Bob’s Hilbert spaces, name a finite set of invariants which is already complete.
• Do all this for multi-partite states. In this case even the case of pure states is not obvious.
• Decide whether the set of separable states can be described in terms of a polynomial invariant f, such that f(ρ) ≥ 0 is equivalent to separability.

accepted.question_text: For pure bipartite-state transformations under local quantum operations and classical communication, Nielsen’s majorization criterion decides when one state A can be converted to another state B. Because some conversions become possible only after tensoring both states with a suitable entangled catalyst C, give an efficient criterion for deciding when there exists a catalyst C such that A tensor C can be converted to B tensor C.
accepted.context_brief: Catalytic majorization criterion

evidence.quote: Using Nielsen’s criterion one can show [JP1] that the following strange situation can happen: state A cannot be converted to state B, but A ⊗ C can be converted to B ⊗ C, where C is a suitably chosen entangled state, the ”catalyst”.
The problem is to give a similarly efficient criterion to decide which pure bipartite states can be converted into each other using a catalyst.

Thus we would like to characterize the order relation “catalytic majorization”:
For some r, (p⊗r) is more mixed than (q ⊗r) in the sense of majorization.

accepted.question_text: Among two-qubit density operators with a fixed spectrum, the same states maximize entanglement of formation, relative entropy of entanglement, and negativity. Is the same maximizing family obtained for every entanglement monotone, and what happens in higher-dimensional systems or under weaker spectral constraints such as fixing only the largest eigenvalue or the entropy?
accepted.context_brief: Maximally entangled mixed states at fixed spectrum

evidence.quote: Among all density operators of two qubits with the same spectrum one may look for those maximizing some measure of entanglement. It turns out [VAM] that for ‘entanglement of formation’, ‘relative entropy of entanglement’ and ‘negativity’ one gets the same “maximally entangled states”.

Is this true for arbitrary entanglement monotones?
Obvious variants of this problem are for higher dimensional systems and weaker constraints on the spectrum, e. g., largest eigenvalue or entropy.

accepted.question_text: A nice error basis is an orthogonal basis of d squared unitary operators on a d-dimensional Hilbert space whose products are basis elements up to phases, inducing an index group. A shift-and-multiply basis is obtained, in a suitable Hilbert-space basis, from products of permutation operators and multiplication operators. Is every nice error basis of shift-and-multiply type?
accepted.context_brief: Classification of nice error bases

evidence.quote: The question that arises here is to decide whether every nice error basis is of shift and multiply type.

An answer to the question, given above, has recently be found by Andreas Klappenecker and Martin Roetteler. They show in their article “On the monomiality of nice error basis” [4] that there is in fact a nice error basis which is not of shift and multiplier type.

accepted.question_text: For the entanglement of formation EF, defined as the infimum over convex decompositions of a bipartite density operator into states of the average von Neumann entropy of Alice’s reduced state, does tensor-product additivity always hold? That is, for any two bipartite density operators rho^(1) and rho^(2), when their tensor product is viewed as a bipartite state by grouping Alice’s two systems and Bob’s two systems, is EF(rho^(1) tensor rho^(2)) always equal to EF(rho^(1)) + EF(rho^(2))?
accepted.context_brief: Additivity of entanglement of formation

evidence.quote: The entanglement of formation [BD96] is one of the standard measures of entanglement. It is defined, for any density operator ρ on a bipartite system, as EF(ρ) = inf (Σi ri S(ρi|A) | Σi riρi = ρ), where S(.) denotes the von Neumann entropy and ρ|A denotes the restriction of a density operator ρ to the “Alice” subsystem (partial trace over the other subsystem), the ρi are density operators and the ri are positive, adding up to one.

Then it is easy to show (by plugging the tensor product of the optimal decompositions of the factors into the variational expression and using the additivity of the entropy) that EF(ρ) ≤ EF(ρ(1)) + EF(ρ(2)).
The problem is to show that equality always holds here.
This problem has been shown to be equivalent to problem 10.

accepted.question_text: For a two-qubit quantum state rho, the relative entropy of entanglement ER(rho) is the infimum of the quantum relative entropy S(rho||sigma) over sigma in the convex set of separable states or in the convex set of states with positive partial transpose. Find a closed formula for ER(rho) for two-qubit systems.
accepted.context_brief: Two-qubit formula for relative entropy of entanglement

evidence.quote:
For a state ρ it is defined as [1]
ER(ρ) = inf
σ∈D
S(ρ||σ),
where D stands for the convex sets of separable or PPT states, and S(.||.) is the quantum relative entropy. The problem is to find a closed formula for this quantity for systems consisting of two qubits.
So far, there is no published solution to the problem.

accepted.question_text: For bipartite density matrices, the spectrum of every separable state is majorized by the spectra of its subsystem reductions. Determine how this majorization criterion fits into the implication chain of separability criteria, in particular whether the reduction criterion implies majorization by the reductions.
accepted.context_brief: Majorization in separability criteria

evidence.quote: The problem is to find out how majorization enters into the known implication chain of separability criteria.
The intuition may be, that all these criteria a strictly stronger than majorization, however the matter is not decided yet.
The answer to the question is contained in [6], stating that the reduction criterion does imply majorization.

accepted.question_text: For quantum channels T1 and T2, let chi(T) be the Holevo quantity obtained by maximizing the output entropy of an ensemble average minus the ensemble average of output entropies over input ensembles. Is chi additive under tensor products, meaning chi(T1 tensor T2) = chi(T1) + chi(T2), or is there a counterexample? Equivalently, can entanglement between signal states ever increase the classical information capacity of memoryless quantum channels beyond the single-letter Holevo expression?
accepted.context_brief: Additivity of Holevo classical capacity

evidence.quote: For each quantum channel T (in the Schrödinger picture), define χ(T) = sup H(Σi piT(ρi)) − Σi piH(T(ρi)), where the supremum is over all probability vectors p = (p1, . . . , pn), and all collections of input states {ρ1, . . ., ρn}, and H denotes the von Neumann entropy.
Show that χ(T1 ⊗ T2) = χ(T1) + χ(T2), or else give a counterexample.
This problem can also be paraphrased as “Can entanglement between signal states help to send classical information on quantum channels?”.

accepted.question_text: For completely positive maps T from trace-class operators to Schatten p-class operators, decide whether maximal output p-norm multiplicativity holds globally, especially for 1 <= p <= 2: is the maximal output p-norm of T1 tensor T2 always equal to the product of the maximal output p-norms of T1 and T2? This related conjecture would imply additivity of minimal output entropy as p decreases to 1 and is tied to the additivity of the Holevo quantity and entanglement of formation.
accepted.context_brief: Multiplicativity of maximal output p-norms

evidence.quote:
If the conjecture is valid, then the additivity of χ tentatively relies upon yet another hypothetical property of multiplicativity of norms of the completely positive mappings
T : ℓ1(H) → ℓp(H); p ≥ 1
By letting p ↓ 1 this implies additivity of the minimal output entropy
The standing conjecture is that multiplicativity holds globally at least for 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, but even the case p = 2 is difficult

accepted.question_text: Regard the quantum capacity of a noisy quantum channel as a function on the space of channels. Is this function continuous, for example with respect to the completely bounded norm: whenever two channels are close in channel distance, must their quantum capacities also be close?
accepted.context_brief: Continuity of quantum channel capacity

evidence.quote: The quantum capacity of a noisy quantum channel can be regarded as a function on the space of all channels. Is this function continuous? In other words: If the distance (e.g. with respect to the cb-norm) between two channels is small, is the distance between the corresponding capacities small as well?
In [1] it was shown that the quantum capacity as a function of the channel is lower semi-continuous.

accepted.question_text: In quantum field theory, vacuum fluctuations can maximally violate CHSH-Bell inequalities for suitable spacelike separated observables, with the violation tending to zero as the localization regions move apart. For a massive scalar free relativistic Bose field, is some nonzero Bell-inequality violation still possible for regions at arbitrarily large separation?
accepted.context_brief: Long-range Bell violation in vacuum correlations

evidence.quote: It is well known [SW] that vacuum fluctuations maximally violate the CHSH-Bell inequalities for suitable spacelike separated observables, and that this violation goes to zero as the two localization regions are moved apart.
Decide whether some (necessarily small) violation of the inequalities is possible for regions arbitrarily far apart. For definiteness, consider a massive scalar free relativistic Bose field.
But the problem as stated above remains open.

accepted.question_text: For a D-dimensional Hilbert space, determine the maximum number K of orthonormal bases that are mutually unbiased, meaning that every vector from one basis has squared inner-product magnitude 1/D with every vector from another basis. It is known that K = D + 1 can be achieved when D is a prime power; decide what happens for other composite dimensions, in particular whether seven mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension six.
accepted.context_brief: Mutually unbiased bases in composite dimensions

evidence.quote: Determine the maximal number K of orthonormal bases in a D-dimensional Hilbert space, which are mutually unbiased in the following sense: If eki denotes the ith vector of the kth basis, all scalar products heki, enj i with k 6= n have the same absolute value (namely D−1/2).

It is known that if D is the power of a prime, K = D+ 1 can be reached, but this is not known for any other composite number. So the problem is already to decide whether there exist K = 7 mutually unbiased bases in D = 6 dimensions.

accepted.question_text: Let E be an e-dimensional vector space of error operators acting on an n-dimensional Hilbert space H. A quantum code C is a subspace whose projector PC satisfies PC A* B PC = lambda(A,B) PC for all A and B in E. For given e and n, find the largest dimension c(e,n) that can always be guaranteed for such a correcting code without knowing more about E, and find tough error models for which this lower bound is nearly tight.
accepted.context_brief: Worst-case dimensions of quantum error-correcting codes

evidence.quote: An error model E is an e-dimensional vector space of operators acting on an n-dimensional Hilbert space H. A quantum code is a subspace C ⊂ H, and is said to correct E, if the projector PC onto C satisfies PC A∗BPC = λ(A, B)PC for all A, B ∈ E, and suitable scalars λ(A, B).

• Given e and n, find the largest c = c(e, n) such that we can assert the existence of a code C of dimension c without further information about E.
• Find “tough error models” for which this bound is (nearly) tight.

accepted.question_text: For a mixed state rho on an NM-dimensional Hilbert space, characterize exactly those spectra for which no factorization of the Hilbert space into an N-dimensional tensor an M-dimensional subsystem makes rho nonseparable. Equivalently, determine from the spectrum alone when every such bipartite factorization leaves rho separable.
accepted.context_brief: Separability determined only by spectrum

evidence.quote: For a mixed state ρ on an NM-dimensional Hilbert space: Are there any factorizations into an N tensor an M dimensional space with respect to which the state is not seperable? This depends only on the spectrum of ρ and the problem is to characterize the spectra for which the answer is ”no”.

The question arises in the context where we are given a highly mixed state on two quantum systems and the ability to apply any unitary operator. Can an inseperable state be obtained? For sufficiently mixed states, this is not possible.

accepted.question_text: For an m-qubit pure state psi, study the asymptotic algorithmic gate complexity of preparing n copies |psi>|psi>... as a function of n and of the gate complexity of preparing one copy of |psi> from |0>. Using a gate set such as Pauli-product rotations with cost |phi|, can the n-copy preparation ever be asymptotically more efficient, for example by cloning a known state, than repeated independent preparation?
accepted.context_brief: Algorithmic complexity of preparing product states

evidence.quote: What can be said about the algorithmic complexity of preparing |ψi|ψi. . . (n times), asymptotically, as a function of n and the algorithmic complexity of preparing |ψi?
By algorithmc complexity I mean the number of gates required to prepare the state from |0i. This depends on the gate set used so the question concerns asymptotics.
It may be possible to clone |ψi more efficiently than to prepare it, given that one knows |ψi.

accepted.question_text: For quantum channels S and T, define CE(T,S) as an entanglement-assisted asymptotic simulation capacity: the supremum of rates r for which many parallel copies of one channel can simulate many copies of the other using arbitrary coding, decoding, and any needed shared entanglement with vanishing error. Is entanglement-assisted coding reversible for all channel pairs, in the sense that CE(T,S) equals the reciprocal of CE(S,T)?
accepted.context_brief: Reverse Shannon theorem for entanglement-assisted coding

evidence.quote:
For any two quantum channels S and T , define the entanglement assisted capacity CE(T, S) of T for S-messages as the supremum of all rates r such that, for large n, rn parallel copies of T may be simulated by n copies of S, where the simulation involves arbitrary coding and decoding operations using (if necessary) arbitrarily many entangled pairs between sender and receiver, and where the errors go to zero as n → ∞.
Show that CE(T, S) = CE(S, T )−1.
The problem is solved for the special case of a known “tensor power source”, i. e. a source emitting the same, known, density matrix at each time step.

accepted.question_text: For every two-qubit state sigma, prove the bi-negativity inequality that the partial transpose, with respect to the second subsystem, of the operator absolute value of sigma’s partial transpose is positive semidefinite: |sigma^{T2}|^{T2} >= 0.
accepted.context_brief: Two-qubit bi-negativity

evidence.quote:
A little problem introduced in [AMVW02] is the bi-negativity on two qubits: Prove that
|σT2|T2 ≥ 0
holds for every two-qubit state σ. Here, T2 denotes the partial transpose with respect to the second system (see also problem 2) and √ |.| is the operator absolute value, |x| = x∗ x.

accepted.question_text: Find Bell inequalities stronger than the CHSH inequalities for Werner states, in the specific sense that the new inequalities are violated by a wider range of Werner states than CHSH is.
accepted.context_brief: Bell inequalities stronger than CHSH for Werner states

evidence.quote: Find Bell Inequalities which are stronger than the CHSH inequalities in the sense that they are violated by a wider range of Werner states.

Recently, Daniel Collins and Nicolas Gisin [CG] found a Bell Inequality and states which violate the new but not the CHSH inequalities. Alas, the range of Werner states violating the new inequality is smaller than that for the CHSH setting.

accepted.question_text: For bipartite entanglement manipulation in the asymptotic limit, local operations and classical communication are irreversible for mixed states, while more general positive-partial-transpose-preserving operations might restore reversibility. Are PPT-preserving operations sufficient for asymptotically reversible interconversion of all pure and mixed bipartite entangled states? If so or if not, what is the smallest nontrivial operation class that permits such asymptotically reversible interconversion for all bipartite entangled states?
accepted.context_brief: Reversible entanglement manipulation under PPT operations

evidence.quote: Asymptotic reversibility under a class of operations would lead to a unique entanglement measure and impose a unique ordering on entangled states thereby playing a role similar to entropy in thermodynamics.

The following are open questions:
• Are ppt-operations sufficient to ensure asymptotically reversibly interconversion of all, i.e. pure and mixed, bi-partite entangled states [BFC]?
• What is the smallest non-trivial class of operations that permits asymptotically reversibly interconversion of all, i.e. pure and mixed, bi-partite entangled states [Bet]?

accepted.question_text: Can there exist bipartite density operators rho1 and rho2 such that neither rho1 nor rho2 violates any CHSH Bell inequality individually, but their tensor product rho1 tensor rho2 does violate a CHSH Bell inequality?
accepted.context_brief: Bell violation activated by tensor products

evidence.quote: Can one find bipartite density operators ρ1,2, neither of which violates any CHSH Bell inequality, with the property that ρ1 ⊗ ρ2 does?

accepted.question_text: Fix an arbitrary probability measure on pure states of a d-dimensional quantum system. Let F(N,M) be the optimal average single-copy fidelity of N-to-M cloning transformations over all M clones, and let F(N,infinity) be the best mean fidelity obtainable by measuring N input copies and repreparing a state from the measurement outcome. Is lim_{M to infinity} F(N,M) always equal to F(N,infinity)? If not for fixed N, does the equality become true in the limit N to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic cloning versus state estimation

evidence.quote: Fix an arbitrary probability measure on the pure states of a d-dimensional quantum system. Let F(N, M) be the optimal single copy fidelity for N-to-M cloning transformations, averaged with respect to the given probability measure and over all M clones.

On the other hand, let F(N, ∞) be the best mean fidelity achievable by measuring on N input copies of the state, and repreparing a state according to the measured data. The problem is to decide whether one always gets
lim
M→∞
F(N, M) = F(N, ∞).
A weaker, but still interesting version of the problem is whether the above equation becomes true in the limit N → ∞.

accepted.question_text: For every Hilbert-space dimension d, does there exist a symmetric informationally complete POVM: a set of d squared normalized vectors forming equiangular lines, whose associated rank-one projection operators sum to a multiple of the identity and are linearly independent so that every quantum state can be reconstructed from the resulting measurement statistics?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of SIC-POVMs in all dimensions

evidence.quote: A set of d2 normed vectors {|φii}i in a Hilbert space of dimension d constitutes a set of equiangular lines if their mutual inner products |hφi|φj i|2 are independent of the choice of i 6= j.

A POVM that arises in this way is called symmetric informationally complete, or a SIC-POVM for short.
The most general form of the problem is: decide if SIC-POVMs exists in any dimension d.

accepted.question_text: For every Hilbert-space dimension d, does there exist a SIC-POVM that is covariant under the d-dimensional Heisenberg, Weyl-Heisenberg, or generalized Pauli group? Equivalently, does there always exist a fiducial vector phi such that the orbit of |phi><phi| under all Weyl operators w(p,q) induces a SIC-POVM?
accepted.context_brief: Heisenberg-covariant SIC-POVMs

evidence.quote:
A vector |φi is called a fiducial vector with respect to the Heisenberg group if the set
{w(p, q)|φihφ| w(p, q)∗}p,q=0...d−1
induces a SIC-POVM. Such a SIC-POVM is said to be group covariant.
The problem: decide if group covariant SIC-POVMs exist in any dimension d.

accepted.question_text: Let the Clifford group be the normalizer of the Heisenberg group in the d-dimensional unitary group, and let z be the Clifford element acting on Weyl operators by z w(p,q) z* = w(q - p, -p). In every dimension d, can a Heisenberg-group fiducial vector for a covariant SIC-POVM be found among the eigenvectors of z?
accepted.context_brief: Zauner’s conjecture for SIC fiducial vectors

evidence.quote:
The normalizer of the Heisenberg group within the unitaries U(d) is called the Clifford group. There exists an element z of the Clifford group which is defined via its action on the Weyl operators as
z w(p, q)z∗ = w(q − p, −p).
Zauner’s conjecture, as formulated in [3], runs: in any dimension d, a fiducial vector can be found among the eigenvectors of Z.

accepted.question_text: Is there a construction linking symmetric informationally complete POVMs to finite affine planes, analogous to constructions that relate finite geometries to mutually unbiased bases?
accepted.context_brief: Finite affine-plane constructions for SIC-POVMs

evidence.quote: Inspired by a construction that links finite geometries to MUBs, there have been some speculations by Wootters about whether SIC-POVMs can be linked to finite affine planes [7].
However, the existence of such a construction remains an open problem.

accepted.question_text: Can every bipartite entangled state be used to generate secret keys, including bound entangled states for which secret key extraction need not proceed by first distilling pure singlets?
accepted.context_brief: Secret key distillation from all entangled states

evidence.quote: Can all bipartite entangled states be used to generate secrete keys?

In [HHHO02] it is shown that some bound entangled states do allow the extraction of a secret key. This is an extreme counterexample to the idea that secret key is best generated from an entangled state by first distilling pure singlets, and using these to get the key.

accepted.question_text: Are two-way distillable entanglement and the secret key rate lockable, meaning extremely sensitive to the loss of a single qubit by one of the partners?
accepted.context_brief: Lockability of operational entanglement and key measures

evidence.quote: Are two-way distillible entanglement and secret key rate lockable?
An entanglement measure is lockable, if it is extremely sensitive to the loss of a single qubit by one of the partners [HHHO04].

accepted.question_text: In the (N, M, K) multipartite correlation setting with no-signalling polytope P, quantum correlation body Q, and classical local polytope C, consider the portion of the boundary of Q that is not already contained in the boundary of P. Can every point on that part of the quantum boundary be reached using K-dimensional local Hilbert spaces and complete von Neumann measurements with K orthogonal projectors on pure states of minimal dimension?
accepted.context_brief: Boundary of the quantum correlation body

evidence.quote: Only obeying no-signalling and positivity constraints, we get the no-signalling polytope P. Contained in it is the convex body Q of correlations obtainable from a multipartite quantum state with quantum mechanical POVM measurements, and inside Q the polytope C of correlations realizable by a classical realistic theory

Problem 26.A:
Consider the part of the boundary of Q, which is not already contained in the boundary of P. Can one reach all these points by choosing each one of the local Hilbert spaces to be K-dimensional, and each measurement as a complete von Neumann measurement (with K orthogonal projectors) on pure states with minimal dimension?

accepted.question_text: In the same no-signalling, quantum, and classical correlation setting, let a proper Bell inequality be a maximal-face inequality of the classical local polytope C that is not also a face of the no-signalling polytope P, so it is not implied merely by positivity and no-signalling. Can every such proper Bell inequality be violated by some quantum correlation data, meaning that Q has points outside the corresponding classical face?
accepted.context_brief: Quantum violation of every proper Bell inequality

evidence.quote:
Problem 26.B:
Consider a maximal face of the polytope C, which is not also a face of P (a blue line in the above figure). In other words, consider a ”proper Bell inequality”, i. e., a tight linear inequality for local classical correlations, which does not follow from positivity and no-signalling.
Then can we find points of Q outside the face? Or, phrased in terms of Bell inequalites, can every proper Bell inequality be violated by quantum correlation data?

accepted.question_text: In the bipartite two-measurement d-outcome Bell setting (N, M, K) = (2, 2, d), show that every face of the local polytope C that is not already contained in a face of the no-signalling polytope P is of CGLMP type, possibly after lifting a lower-dimensional CGLMP inequality by fusing outcomes.
accepted.context_brief: CGLMP completeness for (2,2,d) Bell facets

evidence.quote: In the setting of problem 26, consider especially the case (N, M, K) = (2, 2, d).

Problem 27.A:
Show that every face of the local polytope C, which is not already contained in a face of the no-signalling polytope P is of CGLMP type, i. e., an inequality of the form first written out in [CGLMP], but possibly lifted from lower dimensions by fusing together some outcomes.

accepted.question_text: For the CGLMP inequality in the (2,2,d) Bell setting, prove that the observables that maximally violate the inequality on a maximally entangled state must have the numerically observed form built from computational-basis measurements transformed only by discrete Fourier transforms and diagonal unitaries. Also prove that these measurements achieve the highest resistance of the violation to noise and the best discrimination against classical realism in Kullback-Leibler divergence.
accepted.context_brief: Optimal CGLMP measurements and robustness

evidence.quote:
Problem 27.B:
Numerically, the observables maximally violating the CGLMP inequality on a maximally entangled state are of a very specific form [DKZ], involving measurements in computational basis, transformed by only discrete Fourier transformation and diagonal unitaries [CGLMP].

Show that this is necessarily the case. Show also that these measurements realize the highest resistance of violation to noise, and the best discrimination against classical realism in the sense of Kullback-Leibler divergence [Gill1].

accepted.question_text: For graph states, where vertices represent qubits and edges determine the stabilizer-state phases, decide whether local unitary equivalence always implies local Clifford equivalence. In other words, if two graph states can be mapped into each other by arbitrary tensor products of local unitaries, can they also be mapped into each other by tensor products of local unitaries from the Clifford group?
accepted.context_brief: Local-unitary versus local-Clifford equivalence of graph states

evidence.quote: Decide whether two graph states, which can be mapped into each other by a local unitary, can also be mapped into each other by a local unitary from the Clifford group.
Graph states [Schl] are multiparticle states which are associated with graphs. Each vertex of the graph corresponds to a qubit.
The Clifford group consists of those unitary operators U, such that UPU∗ is a multiple of a Pauli matrix, whenever P is a Pauli matrix.

accepted.question_text: For bipartite Gaussian quantum states, entanglement of formation is defined by minimizing the average pure-state entanglement over all convex decompositions. For certain two-mode Gaussian states this minimum can be achieved using decompositions into pure Gaussian states that are translates of one squeezed Gaussian state with Gaussian weights. Is this true for all Gaussian states, equivalently does Gaussian entanglement of formation equal ordinary entanglement of formation for every Gaussian state?
accepted.context_brief: Gaussian entanglement of formation

evidence.quote: Entanglement of formation is defined as a minimimum over all convex decompositions of a bipartite state into pure states (see problem 7). It has been shown for certain two-mode Gaussian states this minimum can be taken over decompositions of the given state into pure states, all of which are translates of the same squeezed Gaussian state, with Gaussian weights.
Show (or disprove) that this is true for all Gaussian states.
With this, the above question reads: Does Gaussian entanglement of formation equal entanglement of formation for all Gaussian states?
